name: Mandala
summary: Two-player card game of building and destroying mandalas to collect colored sands for set-multiplied scoring.
rules_text: Two players share two mandalas, each with a central Mountain and two side Fields. Setup draws 2 cards to each Mountain, 6 to each hand and 2 face-down to each Cup. On your turn do one: A) Build Mountain: play exactly 1 hand card to either Mountain respecting Rule of Color, then draw to 8 max (max 3). B) Grow Field: play 1+ cards of one color from hand to your own Field of either mandala respecting Rule of Color, keep at least 1 card in hand, draw nothing. C) Discard: discard 1+ cards of one color to discard pile and draw same number. Rule of Color: within one mandala each of the 6 colors may appear in at most one of its three areas. A mandala is complete when all 6 colors appear across its Mountain and both Fields. Then it is destroyed: players alternate drafting colors from its Mountain, starting with player who has more cards in their Fields (tie: player who didn't complete goes first). Drafted colors go to your River and Cup: first card of a new color occupies next River slot 1-6 in order, extras go face-down to Cup; if color already in River all go to Cup. If you had no Field cards all drafted cards are discarded. Then discard both Fields and seed Mountain with 2 new cards. Game ends when a 6th River color is added or after one more destruction following a deck reshuffle. Score = sum over colors in River of River-position x Cup count of that color.
rating_reason: Two-player card duel, bluffing and drafting, no spatial board.
reasons: capability: conditional_subsequence: the step list is flat: a whole BLOCK of steps cannot be chosen instead of another block. This is NOT a limit on conditional scoring or conditional updates: a single step can carry a `when` condition and a single operation an `if`, both arithmetic, so 'the poisoner scores if the choices match, otherwise the chooser' is fine
